item.title: reports: per-currency totals
item.brief: Operator request (verbatim): "reports (Python) reads that CSV on stdin and prints per-account totals. It must now total per account and currency: header account,currency,total_cents, rows sorted by account then currency. CSV from the old ledger (no currency column) still works and counts as USD. A malformed currency code in the input makes reports.py print an error to stderr and exit with status 2." Implement this in the reports repository only. Follow the shared contract exactly. Keep python3 -m unittest passing, add tests for the new totals, the no-currency-column fallback, and malformed codes, update README, and commit on the working branch. Do not push.

pr.body: Approach: totals() keys results by (account, currency), reading currency via row.get('currency', 'USD') and validating with re.fullmatch('[A-Z]{3}'); MalformedCurrency is raised and main() turns it into stderr message and sys.exit(2) before anything is written to stdout. render() emits the new header and sorted (account, currency) rows. Key files: reports.py, test_reports.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -I -m unittest -v: 4 tests OK; py_compile OK; manual runs above. Review: one reviewer (agt_01M7W2XWHKK9MEW6SVA3GMVVEY) passed head 8c9f520 with no blocking findings. Assumptions: an empty currency cell in a file that has a currency column is malformed (exit 2). Non-blocking follow-ups: clearer message for short rows ('missing currency'); amount_cents parse errors still raise a traceback (pre-existing); add tests for CRLF and short rows. Callers that parse the two-column output must be updated before this ships.
pr.summary: made reports total per (account, currency). now prints account,currency,total_cents sorted by account then currency; old CSV without currency column counts as USD; malformed currency code -> stderr + exit 2. before: one total per account, EUR and USD summed together (rent -120100); now: rent,EUR and rent,USD separate rows.

item.title: ledger: currency column
item.brief: Operator request (verbatim): "Our books now hold more than one currency. Two repositories need to change together. ledger (Rust) converts a TSV of transactions on stdin into CSV on stdout. Input lines may now carry a fourth column, the ISO 4217 currency code (exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, e.g. EUR); when it is missing the currency is USD. The CSV header becomes date,account,amount_cents,currency and every row gets the currency. A malformed currency code must make ledger print an error naming the line number to stderr and exit with status 2 (other input errors keep exiting with status 1)." Implement this in the ledger repository only. Follow the shared contract exactly. Keep cargo test passing, add tests for the 4-column, 3-column default, and malformed-code cases, update README, and commit on the working branch. Do not push.

ledger: added the optional fourth currency column. Input lines are now date<TAB>account<TAB>amount[<TAB>currency]; a missing column means USD. Output header is date,account,amount_cents,currency with the currency on every row. A malformed currency code (not exactly three uppercase ASCII letters) prints "line N: ..." to stderr and exits 2; other input errors still exit 1. pr.body: Approach: parse_line returns ParseError (Currency vs Other) so main maps the error to exit 2 or 1. parse_currency requires exactly three ASCII uppercase letters after trim. Missing 4th field defaults to USD. Files: src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/ledger.rs, README.md. Checks: cargo test 8/8 pass; clippy -D warnings clean; rustfmt diffs only on untouched pre-existing lines. Review agt_01M7W2ZW6MSNTVE7V75KM5BD0W: pass, no blocking findings. Assumptions/limits: an empty 4th column (trailing tab) is a bad currency (exit 2), not USD; surrounding whitespace in the code is trimmed like the other fields; the header and prior rows are still written before an error exit (pre-existing).
pr.summary: made the export carry currency. now accepts an optional 4th ISO 4217 column (default USD) and emits date,account,amount_cents,currency. before: 3 columns, no currency; now: currency on every row, malformed code exits 2.
